dedupe_keys.name: vadere open source framework for pedestrian and crowd simulation

description: Vadere is an open-source framework for simulating microscopic pedestrian and crowd dynamics in two dimensions, with generic model classes, visualisation and data analysis tools, and the option of adding other systems such as cars or granular flow. It implements the optimal steps model, the gradient navigation model and the social force model, together with a psychological layer, and these models underlie the group's scientific publications. It is developed by Gerta Köster's group at Munich University of Applied Sciences and used by other institutions; related tools on the site include EikMesh, CrowNet and datafold, and applications cover social identity, airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2, behavioural heuristics and guiding pedestrians with mobile apps. Coverage: generic. Access: free downloads, getting-started guides and video tutorials. Licence: open source; the site calls Vadere free, open-source and thoroughly tested. Caveats: two-dimensional scenarios only. Simulation uses: crowd flow, evacuation and infection spread scenarios for stations, venues and public spaces. Related records: the Jülich pedestrian dynamics archive, OpenTraj and MomenTUM.
